fact: 1914年7月31日21时40分，法国社会党领袖、众议员让·饶勒斯在巴黎蒙马特街的羊角面包咖啡馆（Café du Croissant）用餐时，被拉乌尔·维兰（Raoul Villain）隔着窗户开枪击中头部，几乎当场死亡。三天后法国进入战争，饶勒斯生前阻止战争的最后努力随之终止；他死后法国左翼多数转向支持「神圣联合」。

sources.title: Wikipedia, Assassination of Jean Jaurès
sources.quote: The assassination of Jean Jaurès occurred on Friday 31 July 1914. ... He was attacked by Raoul Villain at 9:40 pm while he dined at the Café du Croissant on rue Montmartre in Paris's 2nd arrondissement, close to the newspaper's headquarters. Jaurès was hit by two gunshots: one bullet pierced his skull and killed him almost instantly. ... Following the death of Jaurès, the majority of the French political left rallied to the Sacred Union

sources.title: Wikipedia, Paris in World War I
sources.quote: On July 31, one day before a general mobilization was declared in France, one of the most prominent leaders of the French Left, the socialist politician Jean Jaurès, an outspoken opponent of going to war, was assassinated at the Café Croissant on Montmartre, not far from the offices of the socialist newspaper L'Humanité, by Raoul Villain

fact: 1914年8月2日（星期日）为法国总动员第一日：总统令宣布动员陆海军，并征用补充军队所需的牲畜、车辆与挽具；所有负有兵役义务的法国男子必须按动员手册的规定报到，「否则将受法律最严厉的惩罚」。动员令以张贴公告形式在巴黎及各地公布。

sources.title: Imperial War Museums, Ordre de Mobilisation Générale（动员令海报，帝国战争博物馆藏 Art.IWM PST 12691）
sources.quote: ARMÉE DE TERRE ET ARMÉE DE MER ORDRE DE MOBILISATION GÉNÉRALE Par décret du Président de la République, la mobilisation des armées de terre et de mer est ordonnée, ainsi que la réquisition des animaux, voitures et harnais nécessaires au complément de ces armées. Le premier jour de la mobilisation est le Dimanche 2 Août 1914 ... Tout Français soumis aux obligations militaires doit, sous peine d'être puni avec toute la rigueur des lois, obéir aux prescriptions du FASCICULE DE MOBILISATION

sources.title: Library of Congress, Declarations of War from Around the World: France, Proclamation of the French Government, Aug. 2, 1914（Journal Officiel, 1914-08-02, 7053–54）
sources.quote: This proclamation called upon the French nation to prepare for war, and informed the nation of the official decree initiating the mobilization of the French armed forces. Le Président de la République, R. [Raymond] Poincaré et al., “A La Nation Française”, Journal Officiel de la République Française, August 2, 1914, Partie Officielle, 7053–54

fact: 1914年8月3日18时45分，德国驻巴黎大使在离任觐见时向法国总理兼外长维维亚尼递交照会，宣布德法处于战争状态；同日法国总统令召集议会于8月4日举行非常会议。

sources.title: Library of Congress, Declarations of War from Around the World: France, Letter from the German Ambassador in Paris to René Viviani, Aug. 3, 1914（Documents Diplomatiques 1914, 149）
sources.quote: This letter from the German Ambassador declared a state of war between Germany and France. Lettre remise par l’Ambassadeur d’Allemagne à M. René Viviani, Président du Conseil, Ministre des Affaires étrangères, au cours de son audience de départ, le 3 août 1914, à 18 h. 45

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica, Austria-Hungary: The outbreak of war
sources.quote: On August 3 Germany declared war against France. In the night of August 3–4 German forces invaded Belgium.

fact: 1914年8月4日至9月6日的边境战役中，法军在洛林与阿尔萨斯的进攻被击退；8月22日是法国军事史上单日死亡最多的一天，超过2.7万名法军士兵在24小时内阵亡。到8月底法军已阵亡约7.5万人，战役期间法军伤亡约26万人（其中约7.5万人死亡），协约国一方总伤亡超过20万。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica, Battle of the Frontiers
sources.quote: August 22, 1914, marked the greatest single loss of life in French military history, with more than 27,000 French soldiers killed in a single 24-hour period. ... Losses: Allied, more than 200,000 casualties of 1,500,000

sources.title: Wikipedia, Battle of the Frontiers
sources.quote: By the end of August, the French Army had suffered 75,000 dead, of whom 27,000 were killed on 22 August. French casualties for the first month of the war were 260,000 ... During the battle, French casualties were c. 260,000 men, of whom c. 75,000 men were killed.

fact: 第一次马恩河战役于1914年9月6日至12日进行：9月3日加列尼识破德军第一集团军转向巴黎以东，命令莫努里第六集团军准备攻击其暴露的右翼；9月6日协约国左翼全线转入反攻，9月9日德军第二集团军后撤，9月10日德军全线退至埃纳河以北并开始掘壕，此后西线进入堑壕战。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica, First Battle of the Marne
sources.quote: First Battle of the Marne, (September 6–12, 1914), an offensive during World War I by the French army and the British Expeditionary Force (BEF) against the advancing Germans ... On September 10 the Germans began a general retreat that ended north of the Aisne River, where they dug in ... where trench warfare set in after assaults by the Allies in the latter half of September (First Battle of the Aisne).

fact: 1914年8月30日，一架德军飞机飞临巴黎投下三枚炸弹，分别落在雷科莱街、瓦尔米河岸与维奈格里街，最后一枚炸死一名老妇、伤三人；9月1日另一次投弹炸死一人、伤十六人。巴黎当局不允许报纸提及这些伤亡，空袭消息被压住。

sources.title: Wikipedia, Paris in World War I
sources.quote: On 30 August, a German plane appeared over Paris and dropped three bombs, one on the Rue des Récollets, one on the Quai de Valmy and the third on the Rue des Vinaigriers; the last bomb killed an elderly woman and wounded three persons. City authorities did not allow the casualties to be mentioned in the press. ... a third plane appeared on September 1, this time to drop more bombs that killed one person and injured sixteen. These casualties were also concealed from the public.

fact: 1914年8月2日，法国总统普恩加莱签署法令，将全国86个省、贝尔福地区与阿尔及利亚三省置于戒严状态（état de siège）；依据1849年法律第8条，警察权与维持秩序权整体移交军事当局，平民可被军事法庭审判，集会、搜索与出版物管制由军方决定。该状态维持到战争结束。

sources.title: 1914-1918-online. International Encyclopedia of the First World War, Martial Law（Steven R. Welch）
sources.quote: On 2 August 1914, the first day of general mobilization, French President Raymond Poincaré (1860-1941) signed a decree that placed all of France under a state of siege. This decree concentrated power in the hands of the military leadership, both in the frontier war zone as well as throughout the rest of France. All of France was in effect under martial law.

sources.title: Clinton Rossiter & William J. Quirk, The State of Siege in Fact: The First World War（Routledge 2002）章节摘要
sources.quote: The state of siege which was declared by the decree of August 2, 1914 in the 86 French departments, the territory of Belfort, and the three departments of Algeria was maintained for the duration of the war. The outbreak of the war was accompanied by an immediate application of article 8 of the law of 1849.

fact: 1914年8月起，法国所有外国人都必须持有居留证；德国与奥匈籍居民被从东北部与要塞区撤离。巴黎另行宵禁：设防城墙各城门18时至次日6时关闭并有守卫，警察厅7月29日令酒馆20时、餐馆21时关门，舞会禁止，大部分煤气灯与路灯熄灭以实行灯火管制。

sources.title: Wikipedia, 1914 French mobilization（Restriction of freedoms）
sources.quote: German and Austro-Hungarian residents were evacuated from the North-East and from the strongholds; all foreigners were required to have a residence permit. In Paris, exceptional measures were taken: the gates of the fortified city walls were closed and guarded from 6 p.m. until 6 a.m.; by order of the Prefecture of Police on July 29, drinking establishments had to close at 8 p.m. and restaurants at 9 p.m.; dances were forbidden; most gas burners and electric streetlamps were switched off as part of a blackout.

fact: 法国政府对一切流通票据实行延期支付：延期自1914年8月1日起至9月1日，后经一系列法令延长至1915年3月1日；法兰西银行于1914年8月5日停止兑现贵金属。法国的私人黄金出口迟至1915年7月3日才由法令禁止、1915年11月15日由法律禁止，1914年内并无全面禁运。

sources.title: William Adams Brown Jr., Breakdown, 1914-1918（NBER, 1940）第一章
sources.quote: The French government imposed a moratorium on all negotiable instruments between August 1 and September 1, which was subsequently extended by a series of decrees to March 1, 1915. ... The Russian State Bank suspended specie payments on July 27, 1914, the Reichsbank on August 4, 1914, and the Bank of France on August 5, 1914. ... The private export of gold from France was not prohibited until July 3, 1915 by decree and November 15, 1915 by law.

fact: 巴黎交易所于1914年7月底停市（一说7月26日、一说8月1日起），8月中旬曾短暂恢复现货交易，9月2日至3日再度关闭，12月7日（一说12月14日）重开。各研究对具体日期口径不一，但「7月底关闭—8月短暂现货—9月初再关—12月初重开」的次序一致。

sources.title: Jopp, One Asset, Two Prices: The case of the Tsarist Repudiated Bonds（表注：巴黎交易所关闭区间）
sources.quote: The London Stock Exchange remained closed between 31 July 1914 and 4 January 1915. The Paris Stock exchange remained closed between 1 August and mid-August 1914, and then again between 2 September and 14 December 1914.

sources.title: Kim Oosterlinck et al., One Asset, Two Prices（会议论文，述巴黎交易所重开日）
sources.quote: The London Stock Exchange closed on July 31, 1914 and the Paris Bourse on September 3, 1914. ... different legislative steps were undertaken for the reopening of the London stock exchange on January 4, 1915 (Michie, 1999) and the Paris Bourse on December 7, 1914.

fact: 1914年9月15日，法国政府设立「国防债券」（bons de la défense nationale）：短期国库券，票息5%，面额100、500与1000法郎，政府最初只希望筹到9.4亿法郎，结果到11月底即已达成，随后把发行上限提高到14亿法郎；法兰西银行同意贴现这些债券。

sources.title: Di Jorio, Oosterlinck & Pouillard, Advertising, Propaganda and War Finance: France and the US during WWI（EBHA 2008）
sources.quote: On September 15, 1914 the government created a new short term bond the so-called “bon de la défense nationale”. These bills had a maturity of 3, 6 or 12 months, paid a coupon of 5% and were issued with face values of 100, 500 and 1000 FF ... The government hoped at first to raise 940 millions thanks to these bills. The sales were however unexpectedly successful and by the end of November 1914 this amount had already been obtained. As a consequence, the upper limit of the issue was raised to 1 400 million FF

fact: 法国在1914年没有发行长期战争公债：四次「国防公债」大发行分别在1915、1916、1917、1918年。1914年靠短期国防债券周转，该年募集16.188亿法郎，到1918年12月31日流通额约220亿法郎。

sources.title: BNP Paribas Histoire, The CNEP issues the National Defence Bonds
sources.quote: Faced with the exceptional financial needs related to the length of the conflict, the French government launched 4 major “National Defence loans” (1915, 1916, 1917 and 1918). ... These short-term loans, issued by the National Treasury starting in 1914, offered subscribers a limited remuneration and the government a few months of financing.

sources.title: Hew Strachan, To Arms（Oxford, 2001）引文页（国防债券发行额）
sources.quote: National defence bonds raised 1,618.8 million francs in 1914, 7,985.8 million in 1915, 12,372 million in 1916,12,630.7 million in 1917 and 16,429 million in 1918. ... On 31 December 1918 22,000 million francs were in circulation.

fact: 面包是法国战时少数价格几乎不变的商品，每公斤售价约43至50生丁（0.43—0.50法郎）。1914年面粉库存与磨坊被征用；1914年8—9月因开战初期的混乱出现过一轮涨价，此后到1915年春通胀受到控制。

sources.title: 1914-1918-online. International Encyclopedia of the First World War, Food and Nutrition (France)
sources.quote: Bread, one of the only commodities whose price remained practically unchanged throughout the conflict (at forty-three to fifty centimes per kilogram) was, in the French context, the ultimate test of the state’s capacity to face food shortages. Stocks of flour and mills were requisitioned in 1914 ... After a period of price increases in August-September 1914 that were linked to the chaos of the first weeks of war, inflation remained contained until the spring of 1915

fact: 据 Laura Lee Downs 的研究，巴黎战前靠每天8—11法郎维持的家庭，到1914年秋只能靠每天4—5法郎生活，而基本商品价格上涨近三分之一；巴黎女工在军工厂每周工作六天、每天7时到18时45分，中间只有半天休息。

sources.title: The French History Podcast, The Munitionettes of World War I（引 Laura Lee Downs）
sources.quote: As Laura Lee Downs recounts, in Paris, “under the best of circumstances, households that had gotten by on Fr 8-11 a day before the war were now struggling to subsist on Fr 4-5 while the cost of basic goods had risen nearly a third [by the Fall of 1914].” ... French women worked extremely long hours starting at 7:00am and lasting until 6:45pm six days a week with a half day on Sunday.

fact: 1914年9月7日至8日，约600辆巴黎出租车把约3000名步兵运到马恩河前线，增援莫努里的第六集团军；这是战争史上第一次用汽车成建制输送部队。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica, First Battle of the Marne
sources.quote: On September 7 and 8, Maunoury's forces were reinforced by about 3,000 infantrymen who were transported to the battle from Paris by some 600 taxis, the first automotive transport of troops in the history of war.

fact: 1914年8月26日起，载着比利时难民的一列列火车抵达巴黎北站，难民被安置在马戏场（Cirque de Paris）；同日加列尼被召回并任命为巴黎军事总督，组织城防。难民潮与前线伤员后送同时压向巴黎的收容与医疗系统。

sources.title: Wikipedia, Paris in World War I
sources.quote: On 26 August, trainloads of refugees from Belgium arrived at the Gare du Nord and were given shelter at the Cirque de Paris. ... On August 26, the same day that the refugees from Belgium began arriving in the city, General Joseph Gallieni was called from retirement and appointed military governor of Paris
